_README.what: PHBR3 Chapter 3 priesthood TEMPLATES. Selecting one populates the Specialty Priest fields on the Core tab and the faith fields on Details. It is a STARTING POINT, not a binding: p.40 tells the DM outright he may change races allowed, proficiencies, rights, weapon and armor restrictions, other limitations and spheres of influence. Edit anything after applying and the provenance field records 'X (Modified)'.
_README.notFields: Deliberately NOT carried: spheres, granted powers, followers and strongholds, proficiency lists, duties, symbols. Those are either recorded elsewhere on the sheet, or are the material p.40 expects to be rewritten. Thirteen fields here, all of which map to a control that already exists.
_README.deityName: A template never touches patron_deity. That field holds the god's NAME - 'Kyros' - not his attribute. The template records 'War' in the provenance field and leaves the name to the player.
_README.blankIsData: An EMPTY string is a positive statement, not an absence. restrictDiet:'' means this priesthood imposes no dietary restriction, and re-applying a template blanks any field the player had filled. hitDie:'' means the standard eight-sided die.
_README.transcriptionStatus: COMPLETE. All 64 entries transcribed - the 59 statted priesthoods of PHBR3 Chapter 3, with Race split into six (Dwarf, Elf, Gnome, Half-Elf, Halfling, Human) because its weapons, armor, spheres, followers, symbols and allies all vary by race. The Druid and the Cleric are deliberately absent: p.55 gives the Druid four sentences and no stat block, and the Cleric has no Chapter 3 entry at all - both are already classes in the tool. Every value was transcribed from a page image, never from OCR or memory.
_README.combatRatings: PHBR3 p.22 derives these from armor and weapon access, and every entry states its own at the end of the Weapon and Armor Restrictions paragraph - 'All together, these constitute Poor combat abilities.' Transcribe what the entry says; do not re-derive it.
_README.primeReq2: PHBR3 p.13. Wisdom is always the first. Where an entry names a second ability, EITHER at 16 earns +5% experience and BOTH at 16 earns +10%. Where it names Wisdom alone, primeReq2 is ''.
_README.minAbilities: Minimum ability scores required to be a priest of this mythos at all (PHBR3 p.13: 'always Wisdom, and often one other'). An OBJECT keyed by ability rather than a wis/second pair, deliberately: in all six entries transcribed so far the second minimum happens to BE the second prime requisite, but nothing in the book promises that, and an entry requiring a score in an ability that is not a prime requisite would break a coupled shape. Iterate the object; do not assume its contents. The values are ENTRY REQUIREMENTS and are unrelated to the 16s that earn the experience bonus - see primeReq2.
_README.schemaScope: EVERY field a Chapter 3 entry prints that maps to something the sheet has, or plausibly will. Chris's call: these are TEMPLATES and starting points, so the cost of an unused field now is far below the cost of re-reading sixty entries later. A field that has no consumer yet is still worth carrying.
_README.transcriptionCost: This schema means roughly 25 values per entry, pulled from prose rather than tables. Budget accordingly - ten entries is a session, not a coffee break.
_README.spheres: The high-value pair: sphere access is a STORED PER-CHARACTER MAP the player otherwise fills by hand, twenty-odd rows at a time. NAMES MUST MATCH getAllSpheres() EXACTLY, which derives them from the loaded spell data rather than from a fixed list -- Title Case, and verified against a live console call, not against PHB_CORE_SPHERES. THERE IS NO 'Elemental' ROW: the data splits it into Elemental Air/Earth/Fire/Water, and PHBR3's 'Major Access to Elemental' is expanded to all four here at transcription time, per the ELEMENTAL_SPHERES note in tables.js that a DM granting Elemental grants all four. 'All' IS DELIBERATELY OMITTED from every entry even though every priesthood has it: it renders as static 'Always' text with no select, because no deity grants it and it cannot be switched off. TWO TRAPS FOR TRANSCRIPTION: 'War' is both a sphere and a priesthood, and they are unrelated -- the War priesthood's spheres are Combat and Elemental, not War. And the eleven Tome of Magic spheres (Chaos, Law, Numbers, Thought, Time, Travelers, War, Wards) POSTDATE PHBR3, so a Chapter 3 entry can never reference one; if a transcription produces one it is an error.
_README.alignmentField: The PRIEST'S permitted alignments, not the deity's and not the flock's - entries print all three and only the first constrains a player character.
_README.permittedVsRestricted: weaponsPermitted / armorPermitted hold the book's RAW lists. restrictWeapons / restrictArmor hold the short human summary that reaches the banners. Both, deliberately: the summary is what a player reads, the raw list is what any future check needs.
_README.orientalWeapons: CONDITIONAL permission - 'Oriental Campaigns: Also bo stick.' Never fold these into weaponsPermitted, or every priesthood silently gains them.
_README.nullVsEmpty: null MEANS NOT TRANSCRIBED. An empty array or string means THE BOOK SAYS NONE, and is a positive statement. Community's alignment:[] records that a civic deity's priests may be of ANY alignment; peace's spheresMajor:null records only that nobody has read that paragraph yet. Conflating the two is how a half-read entry looks finished.
_README.alignment: Keys from ALIGNMENTS in tables.js - lg ln le ng tn ne cg cn ce. THE PRIEST'S permitted alignments only: entries print the deity's, the priest's and the flock's, and only the middle one constrains a player character. [] means unrestricted, not unknown.
_README.weaponsChoose: PHBR3 has three weapon grammars and a flat list cannot hold them. weaponsPermitted is what the priest definitely gets. weaponsChoose, null on most entries, is a pick-N-from-a-list: {count, from, constraint, chosenBy}. chosenBy is 'dm' or 'player' - Community's two extra weapons are the DM's call, War's specialization weapon is the player's.
_README.grantedPowers: A CLOSED VOCABULARY from Chapter 2 (pp.23-27), which is why every Ch.3 entry names its powers rather than describing them: 'Immunity (as described in the Designing Faiths chapter)'. Each row is {power, level, note}: power is one of the keys below, level is the experience level it arrives at (null = 1st, i.e. available immediately), note carries the entry-specific narrowing, which is where all the real content lives - 'Immunity' alone means nothing without 'to all snake venoms'. KEYS: charmFascination, immunity, inspireFear, shapechanging, turnUndead, defiance, inciteBerserkerRage, languageCommunication, layingOnHands, prophecy, identification, detection, analysis, soothingWord, other. 'other' exists because Chapter 2 says the DM may adapt almost any spell into a granted power, so the list is closed in practice but not in principle - Agriculture's create food & water and heroes' feast are spell-derived and take 'other'.
_README.reversedSpheres: SUPERSEDED by the spheresReversed field - see that entry. Retained only so the earlier wording is not silently lost: the sphere arrays could not originally express reversed-forms-only grants, and they were recorded in entry notes.
_README.druid: THE DRUID IS DELIBERATELY NOT AN ENTRY. PHBR3 p.55 gives it four sentences and no stat block: 'The Druid, too, is a priest of a specific mythos. It has been worked up in more detail than the priests presented here, but is still counted one of their number.' It then lists the priesthoods it resembles - Agriculture, Animals, Earth, Fertility, Life-Death-Rebirth Cycle, Nature and Vegetation. There is nothing to transcribe, and the PHB Druid is already a class in the tool. The Cleric likewise has no Chapter 3 entry at all.
_README.columnBreaks: TWO ERRORS SO FAR HAVE COME FROM COLUMN BREAKS, both on the elemental_forces entry: it was first transcribed under the wrong name and faith type, and then given Earth's followers and symbols. Chapter 3 runs three columns per page and an entry's stat block frequently spans a page turn, so the paragraph physically nearest a heading is often the PREVIOUS entry's tail. Check the field labels, not the position. A THIRD INSTANCE, and the worst: the wind entry seeded at the start of transcription actually held VEGETATION's stat block, taken from the left column of p.90 while the Wind heading sits on p.91. It survived undetected for the whole transcription because the entry was marked partial and never re-read. LESSON: a partial entry is not a safe entry - it is an unverified one, and anything seeded before the surrounding pages were read must be re-read, not merely completed.
_README.spheresReversed: Which of the ALREADY-GRANTED spheres are usable in REVERSED FORMS ONLY. A parallel array rather than a flag on the entry, because it is per-sphere: Disease grants Healing and Necromantic reversed-only but Animal and Weather normally. Names must also appear in spheresMajor or spheresMinor - this narrows a grant, it never adds one. [] means nothing is reversed; null means the entry is not yet transcribed. NOT CONSUMED BY THE APPLIER, which grants the sphere outright - more generous than the book. The sphere access map in the app has no reversed state, so this is recorded for a future consumer and for the DM reading the entry. DOES NOT COVER CONDITIONAL SWAPS: Death lets its EVIL priests substitute major Healing for major Protection, and only then is it reversed-only. That is an option rather than a grant, so it stays in that entry's note, as will anything else the book phrases as a choice.
_README.primeReq2Choice: Where an entry lets the PLAYER pick which ability is the second prime requisite, rather than naming one. {from, minScore, chosenBy}. primeReq2 stays EMPTY on such entries - asserting one of the options would be silently wrong, and the applier would then compute a +5%/+10% tier the character may not be entitled to. Applying such a template leaves Second Prime Requisite unset and the player must choose it himself; the note says so. null on every entry that names a single ability.

That makes it BARRED to the Outlaw and Prophet kits, which exclude priests of Philosophies and Forces. RACES ARE UNUSUALLY NARROW: half-elves and humans only, since the philosophy is about the human race specifically, including half-elves reared among humans. Two extra minor accesses, which the book says is why the Granted Powers are weak - one power only. Priests’ alignment is lawful good or lawful neutral though the philosophy itself is true neutral.

priesthoods.label: Earth
priesthoods.genderNote: Lesser earth-gods are as likely male as female, but the comprehensive god of all the earth is probably female.
nwpRequired: Any one of: Agriculture, Brewing, Mining, Stonemasonry
priesthoods.armorPermitted: All non-magical non-metal armor; all non-magical non-metal shields

grantedPowers.note: Detect grade or slope in passage, 1-5 on 1d6, same as the Dwarf ability. DWARF AND GNOME priests of this faith detect slopes automatically whenever they try
Determine approximate depth underground, 1-3 on 1d6, same as the Dwarf ability. DWARF AND GNOME priests of this faith succeed on 1-5 on 1d6
To all snake venoms

priesthoods.restrictArmor: No metal armor or shields; no magical armor or shields
priesthoods.followers: At 8th level: one fifth-level priest, three third-level priests and six first-level priests of the same order, plus one third-level fighter and seven first-level fighters as guards. May take three priests (only one third-level) and two fighters of his choice on adventures. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 8th level.
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with Druids and the priests of Agriculture, Animals, Fertility, Life-Death-Rebirth Cycle, Nature, Seasons, Sky/Weather and Vegetation.
priesthoods.note: ELEMENTAL SPHERE IS PARTIAL AND ODD: "only spells dealing with dust, stone, rock, mud, and earth, plus transmute metal to wood." Encoded as Elemental Earth, which is the closest the four-way split allows, but transmute metal to wood is an Elemental Earth spell only by courtesy - read this note before trusting the sphere list. WEAPONS were chosen in three types: agricultural/harvesting (scythe), stone-using (slings, primitive maces and axes), and those suggesting heavy beating or pounding of the earth (picks, mauls). Second major-access earth priesthood alongside Elemental Forces, but distinct - this is the god of the WORLD in all its aspects, including weather, volcanoes, earthquakes and flood, and many earth-gods are makers of monsters.

priesthoods.label: Elemental Forces

grantedPowers.note: +2 to all saving throws against all PRIEST spells of the Elemental sphere

priesthoods.restrictClothing: Priestly vestments whenever appearing in public
duties: Education: helping educate the flock in both priestly doings and magical learning
Missions: voyages to observe phenomena and learn about the forces behind them
Vigilance against any beings that might interrupt, divert, or channel great natural forces for their own gain
priesthoods.followers: At 9th level: one fifth-level priest, three third-level priests and six first-level priests of the same priesthood, plus one third-level mage and two first-level mages as consultants, and five first-level fighters as guards. May take two priests, one mage and two fighters on adventures. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 9th level. Part of the stronghold must be a library devoted to elemental magics and the elemental planes; scholars interested in those subjects will visit to learn from it or contribute to it.
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with Darkness/Night, Dawn, Fertility, Fire, Light, Lightning, Love, Magic, Seasons, Sky/Weather, Sun, Thunder and Time.
priesthoods.note: CORRECTED: followers and symbols were briefly copied from Earth’s block, which occupies the left column of p.56 immediately above this entry’s continuation. The real values are on p.57 and differ in every particular - 9th level not 8th, mages as consultants, and Fire/Lightning rather than Snakes/Stones. FIRST TRANSCRIBED AS "Everything" AND AS A GOD. It is ELEMENTAL FORCES and a FORCE - the heading reads "Elemental Forces (Force)" and the alignment paragraph says the forces worshipped "are chaotic in nature". Both errors came from working across a column break; both were caught only by re-reading. All armor and shields permitted, and a wide weapon list - hence Good combat abilities. Crossovers are Priest, General, Wizard. Oriental campaigns add daikyu.

priesthoods.label: Everything
priesthoods.genderNote: Just as likely male as female. A male god will probably have a sky aspect; a female, an earth aspect.

grantedPowers.note: Same as the cleric ability

priesthoods.restrictClothing: Must wear priestly vestments whenever appearing in public
duties: Missions of conversion and education in populations which do not believe in this god’s supremacy
priesthoods.followers: At 8th level: one third-level priest and two first-level priests of the same priesthood, plus one fifth-level fighter, two third-level fighters and twelve first-level fighters as soldiers, and four Normal Men and Women with the Reading/Writing nonweapon proficiency as scribes and recorders. May take one priest, three fighters and two Normal Men and Women on adventures. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 8th level.
priesthoods.relations: At DM discretion, good terms with the priests of the philosophies of Divinity of Mankind and Good, since those are philosophies and not gods. Dislikes the priests of all other gods, and hates the priests of the philosophy of Evil.
priesthoods.note: THE BOOK OFFERS THIS AS A CLERIC REPLACEMENT: "This priestly order is very similar to clerics (though with reduced magic); if you decide to remove clerics from your campaign, based on the advice from the Role-Playing chapter, you may wish to recommend that players who still want to play clerics take this priest-class instead." That advice is Toning Down the Cleric, p.122 - the phbr3.toningDownCleric band. The god of a monotheistic culture: either the creator and only true god, or a powerful god who demands all other gods be demoted to demons, devils or servants. Its priests seek to convert the world, sometimes agitating for and initiating wars.

priesthoods.label: Evil (Philosophy)

grantedPowers.note: Detect good — the reversed detect evil spell — three times per day, in addition to all other spells
Control Undead, same as the evil cleric ability

duties: Missions: spreading evil and misery across the world; their whole lives are spent in missions against happiness, goodness, contentment and beauty
Vigilance against the doings of any good priests, especially priests of the Philosophy of Good
priesthoods.followers: At 9th level: one third-level priest and two first-level priests of the same order, plus one fifth-level fighter, three third-level fighters and six first-level fighters as soldiers, and one third-level thief and two first-level thieves as special agents. ALL followers will be of the exact same alignment as the priest they follow. May take two priests, two fighters and one thief on adventures. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 9th level. Temples of Evil typically have torture chambers and trapped dungeons, but this is a tendency, not a requirement of the order.
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with the priests of Disease, and sometimes at DM discretion allied with the priests of Death and Mischief/Trickery. Dislikes the priests of Divinity of Mankind, Everything, Fortune/Luck, Good, Healing, Love, Redemption and Wisdom.
priesthoods.note: SECOND PHILOSOPHY, so BARRED to the Outlaw and Prophet kits, which exclude priests of Philosophies and Forces. Also on the Pacifist, Peasant and Savage kits’ barred lists by name. ALL EVIL ALIGNMENTS BELONG TO THE SAME SECT - unusually, the lawful, neutral and chaotic priests have to cooperate rather than splitting into rival cults as most mixed-alignment priesthoods in this book do. PROTECTION SPHERE IS REVERSED-FORMS-ONLY, which the sphere arrays cannot express - see reversedSpheres in this README. THE BOOK NOTES THIS CONVERTS EASILY into the priesthood of a specific god of evil: no requirement or ability changes, the only difference being that a god’s priest receives orders rather than inventing his own schemes of destruction.

priesthoods.label: Fate, Destiny
priesthoods.genderNote: The god of this attribute is as likely to be male as female.

grantedPowers.note: Commune once per month, even at first level, in addition to all other spells. At first level he can only ask one question per casting

duties: Guidance: the doctrine of acceptance of the will of the gods
Missions against those who defy the gods
Vigilance against those who defy the gods
priesthoods.followers: At 8th level: one fifth-level priest, three third-level priests and sixteen first-level priests of the same priesthood. May take three priests on adventures, only one of them third-level. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 8th level.
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with the priests of Ancestors, Fortune/Luck, Oracles/Prophecy and Time.
priesthoods.note: A PHILOSOPHICAL BUT JOYLESS PRIESTHOOD, in the book’s own words. Preaches predestination and acceptance. When two gods are in opposition these priests do NOT interfere in the mortal struggle - unless one of them is the god of fate/destiny, in which case they support him. When a single god is pursuing a goal and mortals oppose him, they work for the god and AGAINST the mortals, regardless of the god’s motives. The net and lasso were chosen because they represent the inevitability of fate and destiny.

priesthoods.label: Fertility
priesthoods.genderNote: As likely male as female. Those representing animal life are more likely male, those representing plant life more likely female.
priesthoods.armorPermitted: Hide armor and leather armor (normal or magical); all non-metal shields

grantedPowers.note: Never in combat, and only once per day
One species of animal from: cattle, goats, horses, rabbits, sheep, snakes. Gives no CONTROL over the animal — he may merely talk with it

priesthoods.restrictArmor: No metal armor; no metal shields
priesthoods.restrictCelibacy: FORBIDDEN to remain chaste — the priests of the god of Fertility "are not allowed to remain chaste"
duties: Conducting ceremonies which celebrate and promote fertility in all living beings, at the start of spring and at harvest-time, in some places characterized by orgiastic behavior
Vigilance against the doings of the priests of Death
priesthoods.followers: At 9th level: one fifth-level priest, three third-level priests and six first-level priests of the SAME ALIGNMENT, plus fifteen first-level fighters. The fighters act as guards during the more somber rituals but participate in the more chaotic ones. May take one priest (not the fifth-level one) and six fighters on adventures. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 9th level. IN SOME SECTS the fighters are all women of any chaotic alignment, called MAENADS; for others the DM can substitute intelligent wood-beings such as satyrs, centaurs, dryads and nymphs up to 10 HD, who accompany the priest on woodland adventures only. Such beings are not bound to specific trees, can voyage in any forested realm, and when they charm victims there is no chance the victims will disappear forever — after a day in the nymph’s company the victim chooses whether to stay or leave.
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with Druids and the priests of Agriculture, Animals, Birth/Children, Earth, Elemental Forces, Life-Death-Rebirth Cycle, Nature, Seasons, Sky/Weather and Vegetation. Dislikes the priests of Death.
priesthoods.note: THE FILE’S FIRST INVERTED RESTRICTION: not a prohibition but a REQUIREMENT of unchastity - "Priests of the god of Fertility are not allowed to remain chaste." Recorded in restrictCelibacy because that is where a reader will look, but note it runs the opposite way to every other entry in that field. Two extra minor accesses, which the book says is why the Granted Powers are not very strong. ARMOR IS UNUSUALLY SPECIFIC: hide and leather ONLY, but magical versions of those are allowed, where most non-metal priesthoods bar magical armor outright. Followers must share the priest’s exact alignment, as with Evil.

priesthoods.label: Fire
priesthoods.genderNote: Fire-gods are as likely to be male as female.
priesthoods.armorPermitted: All metal armor; all metal shields

grantedPowers.note: Of Restriction/Obstacle — the priest can pass unharmed through any wall of fire spell

+2 saving throw vs. all PRIEST spells of the Elemental sphere, and vs. all WIZARD spells of the Alteration and Evocation schools with the words fire, burning, flaming, pyrotechnics or incendiary in their names

priesthoods.restrictArmor: METAL ARMOR AND SHIELDS ONLY — the inverse of the usual priestly restriction
priesthoods.followers: At 8th level: three third-level priests and six first-level priests of the same order, plus five first-level fighters as guards, one third-level mage and two first-level mages as consultants, and ten Normal Men and Women, half with Reading/Writing proficiency and half with Fire-Starting, who act as temple functionaries. May take two priests (only one third-level), two fighters, one mage and two Normal Men and Women on adventures. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 8th level.
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with the priests of Dawn, Elemental Forces, Justice/Revenge, Light, Lightning, Magic, Metalwork, Race (Dwarf) and Sun. Not fond of, but not enemies of, the priests of Oceans/Rivers. Dislikes the priests of Disease.
priesthoods.note: ELEMENTAL AND SUN ARE BOTH PARTIAL, which is why the priesthood gets extra minor accesses. Elemental is limited to spells whose names include Fire, Flame, Heat, Pyrotechnics, plus chariot of Sustarre; encoded as Elemental Fire, the closest the four-way split allows. THE SUN SPHERE HAS ONLY SIX SPELLS TO START WITH, which the book states as its own justification - a limitation the sphere arrays cannot express at all. ARMOR IS INVERTED: metal only, where every other restricted priesthood in the file bars metal. Fire is the god of the forge as much as the hearth.

priesthoods.label: Fortune, Luck
priesthoods.genderNote: Gods of luck are most likely to be female.
priesthoods.restrictArmor: No armor of any kind; no shields
duties: Missions to bring luck to the unlucky — often required to travel to communities and places suffering a series of bad-luck events and improve matters there
Vigilance against the deeds of the priests of Disease and of the philosophy of Evil, who are always bringing bad fortune to the people
priesthoods.followers: At 7th level: one fifth-level priest, three third-level priests and sixteen first-level priests of the same order. May take three priests on adventures, only one of them third-level. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 7th level.
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with the priests of Competition, Fate/Destiny, Mischief/Trickery and Trade. Dislikes the priests of Evil.
priesthoods.note: A GOD OF GOOD FORTUNE ONLY - explicitly NOT a god of bad luck or ill fortune. Its priests are practical, common-sense people who believe much of luck is self-made; they analyse supplicants’ situations and contrive meetings between people who can help each other. Some adopt a "fairy godmother" attitude and improve peoples’ lot through mischievous meddling. WEAPONS ARE "WEAPONS OF OPPORTUNITY" - the sort a character could make from things found on the road. The priest need not actually find them, but the permitted list reflects that idea.

priesthoods.label: Good (Philosophy)

grantedPowers.note: Detect evil three times per day, in addition to all other spells
Same as the cleric ability
PERMANENT +1 to hit and damage vs. all evil enemies, above and beyond all other bonuses

duties: Missions: ongoing missions against priests of the philosophy of Evil, and against the plots of evil men, priests of the god of disease, and the like
priesthoods.followers: At 9th level: one third-level priest and two first-level priests of the same order, plus one fifth-level paladin, three third-level paladins and six first-level paladins as soldiers, and one third-level mage and two first-level mages as special agents. The priests and mages will be of the EXACT same alignment as the priest they follow; the paladins are automatically lawful good. May take one priest, two paladins and one mage on adventures. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 9th level. Such strongholds are often built with hospitals and libraries as part of their construction, but this is not a requirement of the order.
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with the priests of Divinity of Mankind, Everything, Peace, Race, Redemption and Wisdom. Especially dislikes the priests of Evil.
priesthoods.note: THIRD PHILOSOPHY, so BARRED to the Outlaw and Prophet kits, which exclude priests of Philosophies and Forces. Also named on the Peasant and Savage kits’ barred lists. THE EXACT MIRROR OF EVIL (p.57): both are Good combat, both have a Warrior crossover, both require only Religion, both grant a thrice-daily detect spell plus an undead power, and both put all three of their alignments in ONE SECT rather than splitting into rival cults. THE PERMANENT +1 TO HIT AND DAMAGE vs. evil enemies is unique in the file so far - every other combat bonus in Chapter 3 is situational or spell-derived. It stacks above and beyond all other bonuses. Some chaotic good priests of this philosophy break all sorts of laws and restrictions of society in order to realize their good intentions - they may or may not believe in Law.

priesthoods.label: Guardianship
priesthoods.genderNote: Depends on the culture: if there are few women warriors the god is probably male; if women are often warriors, just as likely female as male.

grantedPowers.note: Infravision, same as the Elf ability. An elven or half-elven priest of this faith has infravision of DOUBLED range, to 120 feet
Same as the paladin ability

priesthoods.restrictWeapons: NO RANGED ATTACKS — the priesthood may use or make no ranged weapon attacks, and may not even throw its spears, javelins, daggers or knives
duties: Missions: a priest of this god is almost always on some sort of mission — to protect a specific person, place or thing. He may have chosen it or been assigned to it, and it may change between adventures
priesthoods.followers: At 8th level: three third-level priests and six first-level priests of the same order, plus five third-level fighters as temple guards. May take three priests (only one third-level) and two fighters on adventures. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 8th level. THE STRONGHOLD MUST be built in the fashion of a castle or fortress, even in a city, and must be constructed so that it can easily repel invasion.
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with the priests of Community, Healing, Strength and War.
priesthoods.note: THE NO-RANGED-ATTACKS RULE IS THE REASON FOR THE WEAPON LIST: "This priesthood represents a god who is a defender, not an aggressor; therefore, the priesthood can use or make no ranged weapon attacks." Javelins and spears are permitted but may only be used in melee - they may not even be thrown. That is a restriction on USE rather than on the weapon itself, which no weapon list can express, so it lives in restrictWeapons. PRIESTS OF THIS SORT DO NOT MAINTAIN TEMPLES for small communities - they spend most of their time on mission, and only at 8th level do they build their own temples and send subordinates out instead. The book flags this as "a great way to get priest-PCs into interesting adventures", since the priesthood provides bodyguards for famous public figures championing causes.

priesthoods.label: Healing
priesthoods.genderNote: Healing gods are as likely to be male as female.

grantedPowers.note: To all poisons and diseases, but only a +2 to his saving throw — not automatic success
Same as the paladin ability
Same as the cleric ability
Of diseases and poisons: on an Intelligence check, which the DM may modify for how common or rare the ailment is, the priest knows what disease or poison afflicts his patient
As analysis, same scope

priesthoods.restrictArmor: No metal armor; no shields
priesthoods.restrictWeapons: Nondamaging weapons only — though many priests end up learning to use the staff, their symbol, as a weapon, and the god assents by not punishing them for it
priesthoods.restrictClothing: Must wear a symbol indicating their calling whenever appearing in public
priesthoods.restrictions: MAY NEVER DELIBERATELY TAKE SENTIENT LIFE. Doing so is a "betrayal of goals" — see PHBR3 p.121. The order is also not allowed to turn away a patient in need; if they can help him, they must
duties: Education: teaching the flock, indeed anyone interested, the arts of medicine, sanitation and healing
Missions to sickness-infested lands to help in the healing process
Vigilance against the activities of the priests of the god of disease
priesthoods.followers: At 7th level: three third-level priests and six first-level priests of the same priesthood, plus thirty Normal Men and Women, all of whom must have the Healing nonweapon proficiency, who act as chirurgeons (doctors) and nurses. May take two priests (only one third-level) and two Normal Men and Women on adventures. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 7th level. THE STRONGHOLD MUST ACT AS A HOSPITAL for the nearest community, and may turn away no patient who has suffered a life-threatening injury or disease.
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with the priests of Birth/Children, Dawn, Guardianship, Light, Love, Peace and Sun. Dislikes the priests of Death, Disease and Evil.
priesthoods.note: THE IMMUNITY IS DELIBERATELY WEAK: +2 to the saving throw rather than automatic success, which is a Low Power immunity in Chapter 2 terms despite covering all poisons AND all diseases. THE NO-KILLING RULE IS THE STRONGEST BEHAVIOURAL RESTRICTION IN THE FILE SO FAR and the book ties it directly to the Betrayal of Goals ladder on p.121 - warning, then divine appearance, then reduction to 1 hit point and forced class change to fighter. THE STAFF EXCEPTION IS EXPLICIT AND CHARMING: nondamaging weapons are the rule, but the staff is the priesthood’s symbol, so many priests learn to use it as a weapon and "the god gives his assent to this knowledge by not punishing them for using the staff in a damaging way."

priesthoods.label: Hunting
priesthoods.genderNote: The god of hunting is as likely to be male as female.

grantedPowers.note: PERMANENT +2 to hit with bows, above and beyond all other bonuses

priesthoods.restrictArmor: No metal armor; no shields
priesthoods.restrictWeapons: The harpoon and trident may ONLY be used by priests whose god is a god of the sea or of fishing. If the god is devoted to land-hunting, its priests cannot use them
duties: Vigilance: protecting the animal-life of the surrounding wilderness against anything that endangers species, including drought, excess hunting and deforestation — though not against hunting itself
priesthoods.followers: At 9th level: one third-level priest and two first-level priests of the same priesthood, plus one fifth-level ranger, three third-level rangers and six first-level rangers as "forest rangers", and ten Normal Men and Women with the VETERINARIAN nonweapon proficiency. May take one priest and two rangers on adventures. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 9th level. The stronghold may be built in a city or the wilderness but must work principally with hunters and their needs.
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with the priests of Animals, Darkness/Night, Light, Moon and Sun.
priesthoods.note: SECOND REQUIRED WEAPON PROFICIENCY IN THE FILE (Bow), after Death’s scythe. THE PERMANENT +2 TO HIT WITH BOWS is the second always-on combat modifier in the file, after Good’s +1 vs. evil, and the larger of the two. INTRODUCES A NONWEAPON PROFICIENCY THAT IS NOT IN THE PLAYER’S HANDBOOK: Veterinarian, which the book defines inline as "identical to the Healing proficiency, except it can only be used to heal animals and monsters." It appears only in the followers list, not in this priesthood’s own required or recommended proficiencies, so nothing needs to resolve it - but it will not match core_nwp.json if anything ever tries. Despite being a patron of hunters, this god is also a protector of animals from needless destruction at the hands of too-greedy hunters and poachers. An alternate aspect would be a god of Fishing. THE HARPOON AND TRIDENT ARE CONDITIONAL on the god’s aspect - permitted only for sea or fishing gods, forbidden to land-hunting ones. A second case, after Guardianship, where weaponsPermitted and restrictWeapons must be read together. DUTIES also include vigilance over the animal population: hunters are not stopped, but anything endangering species - drought, excess hunting, deforestation - brings the wrath of the priesthood.

priesthoods.label: Justice, Revenge
priesthoods.genderNote: The deity of revenge is more likely to be female than male.

grantedPowers.note: Detect lies three times per day, even at first level, in addition to all other spells

priesthoods.restrictions: MAY NOT REFUSE TO INVESTIGATE when a story of injustice is brought to him, unless he has already investigated that same complaint. Refusing, or investigating and then refusing to act on a proven injustice, is a "betrayal of goals" — see PHBR3 p.121. He MAY discover an injustice and then take the time to gather enough influence and force to effect revenge; he does not have to act immediately
duties: Missions to achieve justice when justice has been thwarted
Vigilance: keeping their ears open and keeping track of those who try to avoid the consequences of their actions
priesthoods.followers: At 9th level: three third-level priests and six first-level priests of the same order, plus one third-level fighter, one third-level mage, one third-level illusionist, one third-level thief and one third-level bard who act as consultants. May take three priests (only one third-level), the fighter, the mage, the illusionist, the thief and the bard on adventures. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 9th level. THE STRONGHOLD MUST INCLUDE A COURTROOM and an execution chamber or field — the method of execution is up to the priests.
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with the priests of Competition, Death, Fire and War. Dislikes the priests of Peace. Individual DMs might consider this priesthood to belong to Good or Evil camps, but Good sects consider it too "tainted" to be truly good, while Evil sects dislike that it punishes the wicked.
priesthoods.note: THE PUNISHMENT MUST FIT THE CRIME - "a theft does not warrant the killing of the thief in most cases, for instance." ALIGNMENT IS SINGLE AND FIXED at lawful good, and the deity itself is lawful NEUTRAL - the second entry after Divinity of Mankind where the priests are more constrained than the god. HALFLINGS ARE EXCLUDED, the first entry in the file to bar them while allowing the other five. THESE PRIESTS OFTEN WORK IN SECRET, since they are approached to punish those ordinary laws cannot touch - a rich man who can bribe his way out of any charge. "These vigilante priests are not appreciated by local governments." Completed from p.66: the stronghold must include a courtroom and an execution chamber or field, with the method of execution left to the priests.

priesthoods.label: Life-Death-Rebirth Cycle (Force)

grantedPowers.note: Same as the cleric ability

priesthoods.restrictArmor: No metal armor; no shields
priesthoods.restrictDiet: MAY NOT EAT ANIMAL FLESH — they are vegetarian. Violating this is a MINOR OFFENSE (PHBR3 p.120), so the god withholds some of the priest’s spells the following day
duties: Conducting ceremonies at summer and winter solstice and at spring and autumn equinox, in celebration of the cycle
Education of the flock in the beliefs of the cycle
Comforting the flock with the knowledge that death is merely a point in the cycle and not the end
Protection of the world from forces which might disrupt the cycle
Vigilance against any beings who wish to tamper with the cycle — priests of the philosophy of Evil, or mad gods of death who will not rest until everything is dead forever
priesthoods.followers: At 8th level: one fifth-level priest, three third-level priests and sixteen first-level priests of the same order. May take three priests of his choice on adventures. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 8th level.
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with Druids and the priests of Agriculture, Animals, Death, Earth, Fertility, Nature, Seasons, Sky/Weather and Vegetation. UNDEAD BEINGS ARE THEIR SWORN ENEMIES, having removed themselves from the natural cycle.
priesthoods.note: SECOND FORCE IN THE FILE, so BARRED to the Outlaw and Prophet kits. Also named on the Scholar kit’s barred list. THE RESURRECTION RESTRICTION IS UNIQUE: the Necromantic sphere carries a Special Note that these priests CANNOT use the resurrection spell - they use reincarnate instead. That is a per-SPELL restriction inside a granted sphere, which neither spheresMajor nor spheresReversed can express. Recorded here only. THE FIRST DIETARY RESTRICTION IN THE FILE, and the book grades it explicitly as a MINOR OFFENSE rather than a betrayal - the god withholds some spells the next day (p.120). ALIGNMENT IS SINGLE AND FIXED at true neutral, matching the force itself. THE BOOK WARNS THIS FORCE IS MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE WITH SEPARATE GODS OF DEATH AND FERTILITY: "if the DM has gods of death and fertility in his campaign, he may not have this cycle; if he has this cycle, he may not have those gods." A campaign-design constraint, not a character one.

priesthoods.label: Light
priesthoods.genderNote: This deity is as likely to be male as female.

grantedPowers.note: Infravision, same as the elf ability. An elven or half-elven priest of this faith has infravision of DOUBLED range, to 120 feet
Same as the cleric ability
Same as the paladin ability

priesthoods.restrictArmor: No metal armor; no shields
duties: Vigilance against dark, evil forces such as undead
priesthoods.followers: At 9th level: one fifth-level priest, three third-level priests and six first-level priests of the same order, plus one third-level mage and two first-level mages as consultants, and one third-level fighter and two first-level fighters as guards. May take three priests (only one third-level), one mage and one fighter on adventures. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 9th level.
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with the priests of Arts, Crafts, Darkness/Night, Dawn, Elemental Forces, Fire, Healing, Hunting, Literature/Poetry, Magic, Metalwork, Moon, Music/Dance, Oracles/Prophecy and Sun.
priesthoods.note: THE MOST LEVEL-GATED POWER LIST IN THE FILE SO FAR: five powers arriving at 1st, 1st, 3rd, 5th and 9th level. Chapter 2 (p.23) says a DM may stagger granted powers across levels rather than giving them all at first, and this is the clearest worked example of that. THE WEAPONS ARE ALL RANGED - "representing the god’s ability to strike from afar with inspiration... or stroke." The only melee options are the dagger, knife and spear, which are also throwable. The god is a friend of life, a patron of magic, a proponent of logical thought, and an enemy of the undead. Lesser gods of this attribute would be gods of one aspect of light - one of Reason, another of Inspiration.

priesthoods.label: Lightning
priesthoods.genderNote: The lightning-god is male.

grantedPowers.note: Call lightning once per day, in addition to all other spells, EVEN AT 1ST LEVEL — at 1st level the spell lasts only 1 turn and does 2d8 damage

priesthoods.followers: At 8th level: three third-level priests and six first-level priests of the same priesthood, plus one fifth-level warrior, two third-level warriors and four first-level warriors. May take three priests (only one third-level) and two warriors of his choice on adventures. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 8th level.
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with the priests of Elemental Forces, Fire, Nature, Race (Dwarf), Sky/Weather, Strength and ESPECIALLY Thunder.
priesthoods.note: ELEMENTAL SPHERE IS PARTIAL: only spells whose names include Air, Wind, Fire, Flame, Heat or Pyrotechnics, plus chariot of Sustarre. Encoded as Elemental Air and Elemental Fire, the closest the four-way split allows. Third partial-Elemental case after Dawn and Fire. RACES ARE THE NARROWEST YET FOR A GOD: dwarves, half-elves and humans only - no elves, gnomes or halflings. THIRD REQUIRED WEAPON PROFICIENCY, and the first phrased as a CHOICE rather than a single weapon: warhammer OR hand/throwing axe, player’s choice. wpRequired holds it as a single descriptive string; if weapon proficiency requirements are ever consumed mechanically this will need the weaponsChoose treatment. The god is little concerned with mortal affairs and does not meddle much, but grants power to his priests and has no objection to worship. Evil priests have their own sect.

priesthoods.label: Literature, Poetry
priesthoods.genderNote: The god of literature and poetry is as likely to be male as female.

grantedPowers.note: EVERY LEVEL FROM 1ST TO 8TH the priest receives one extra language of his choice — or, if preferred, an extra nonweapon proficiency slot usable only for languages. The languages chosen may only be those of sentient humanoid races

priesthoods.restrictArmor: No armor of any kind; no shields
duties: Education: encouraging and supporting members of the flock, or of the general population, who show signs of talent with prose or poetry
Vigilance against the human forces of censorship and repression
priesthoods.followers: At 8th level: three third-level priests and six first-level priests of the same order, plus one third-level fighter and two first-level fighters as guards, and twenty Normal Men and Women each with either Reading/Writing or an appropriate Artistic Ability nonweapon proficiency. May take three priests (only one third-level), one fighter and four Normal Men and Women on adventures. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 8th level. THE STRONGHOLD MUST ACT AS A MEETING-PLACE for writers and poets to exchange ideas, and must therefore be built with meeting rooms or even lecture halls dedicated to those rather than to priestly doings.
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with the priests of Arts, Community, Crafts, Culture, Divinity of Mankind, Light, Metalwork, Music/Dance, Sun and Wisdom.
priesthoods.note: THIRD SIX-SIDED HIT DIE in the file, after Peace and Arts and Dawn. THE LANGUAGE GRANT IS BOUNDED DIFFERENTLY FROM PEACE’S: every level from 1st to 8TH here, where Peace runs 1st to 4th. Both restrict the choice to sentient humanoid tongues, and both offer the alternative of a proficiency slot usable only for languages. The sp_language_slot field is a plain yes/no and cannot express either bound - see the note on that field. Very much like the god of Arts, but concerned with reading, writing, recitation, the chronicling of history and the teaching of youth.

priesthoods.label: Love
priesthoods.genderNote: A god of ALL the aspects of love is likely to be female. A god of just one aspect is as likely male as female.

grantedPowers.note: Same as the cleric ability

priesthoods.restrictArmor: No armor of any kind; no shields
priesthoods.restrictCelibacy: MUST BE WED BY 8TH LEVEL. Unless the god is a deity of pure and platonic relationships (DM discretion), a priest may be unmarried when he enters the priesthood at 1st level, but must have married by the time he reaches 8th. Failing to do so denies the god his due and constitutes a "betrayal of goals" — see PHBR3 p.121
duties: Promoting love wherever possible, especially by removing obstacles to it
Interfering to convince families of the rightness of a match when star-crossed youths wish to marry
Counselling spouses into reconciliation when a marriage collapses under distrust or disinterest
Using every means available, from trickery to charm spells, to make a disinterested party fall in love with a more devout character
Vigilance: these priests believe in marriages of love, not of convenience or politics, and conspire to keep young lovers together when their families or social class would part them
priesthoods.followers: At 7th level: three third-level priests and six first-level priests of the same order, plus one third-level mage and two first-level mages as consultants, one third-level fighter and two first-level fighters as guards, and ten Normal Men and Women each with a nonweapon proficiency useful to the temple (Etiquette, Local History and Reading/Writing especially). May take three priests (only one third-level), one mage, one fighter and four Normal Men and Women on adventures. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 7th level. THE STRONGHOLD MUST ACT AS A SANCTUARY for young lovers fleeing the retribution of angry families, and is often built with secret chambers and quarters for those who take sanctuary.
symbols: Girdle (the woman’s belt of the ancient world, not the modern accoutrement)
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with the priests of Birth/Children, Divinity of Mankind, Elemental Forces, Healing, Marriage and Peace. Dislikes the priests of Evil.
priesthoods.note: THE FILE’S FIRST FOUR-SIDED HIT DIE. Chapter 2 p.21 reserves d4 for poor-combat priesthoods of deities whose attribute implies soft living, and warns it should not be automatic - Love is the book’s own worked example. A SECOND INVERTED CELIBACY RULE, and a different shape from Fertility’s. Fertility FORBIDS chastity; Love REQUIRES marriage by 8th level. Both live in restrictCelibacy and both run opposite to the field’s usual sense. FIVE GRANTED POWERS, the joint-most in the file, which is the Chapter 2 compensation rule working as intended: poor combat, d4 hit dice, no armor, and a weapon list of five items. THE WEAPONS were chosen for their appearance in stories about mythological love-gods, or for their usefulness in capturing mates.

priesthoods.label: Magic
priesthoods.genderNote: Gods of magic are as likely to be male as female.

grantedPowers.note: FROM 1ST LEVEL TO 8TH the priest receives one extra language per level — or one extra nonweapon proficiency slot usable only for languages. He may choose the language of any sentient race known to him, OR may choose to communicate with any animal species, with each of these choices
Same as the cleric ability; if EVIL, Control Undead instead
Infravision, same as the elf ability. An elven or half-elven priest of this faith has infravision of DOUBLED range, to 120 feet

priesthoods.restrictArmor: No armor of any kind; no shields
duties: Education: these priests cooperate with magicians to educate in the ways of magic
Acting as scholars of magic — preserving libraries of magical information and encouraging correspondence and the exchange of ideas and spells between mages
priesthoods.followers: At 9th level: three third-level priests and six first-level priests of the same order, plus one fifth-level mage as consultant, and one third-level fighter and seven first-level fighters as guards. May take three priests (only one third-level), one mage and two fighters on adventures. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 9th level.
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with the priests of Darkness/Night, Dawn, Elemental Forces, Fire, Healing, Light, Moon, Oracles/Prophecy and Sun.
priesthoods.note: THE FILE’S SECOND FOUR-SIDED HIT DIE, after Love, and the book states the trade openly: "This priesthood has an extra major access, which helps make up for its reduced hit points." TEN MAJOR ACCESSES for a poor-combat priesthood - the widest sphere access in the file so far. THE LANGUAGE GRANT IS THE BROADEST OF THE THREE: Peace runs 1st to 4th and restricts the choice to sentient humanoid races; Literature/Poetry runs 1st to 8th, same restriction; MAGIC runs 1st to 8th and allows EITHER any sentient race known to him OR communication with any animal species, chosen freshly each level. TURN UNDEAD FLIPS ON ALIGNMENT, as with Darkness/Night: evil priests Control instead of Turn. RACES ARE NARROW: elves, half-elves and humans only. Evil priests have their own sect. The weapons permitted are close to those permitted to mages, since this priest is close in aspect to one.

priesthoods.label: Marriage
priesthoods.genderNote: The god of marriage is as likely to be male as female.
priesthoods.armorPermitted: All non-magical armor; all non-magical shields

grantedPowers.note: Same as the paladin ability
Same as the cleric ability

priesthoods.restrictArmor: No magical armor or shields
priesthoods.restrictCelibacy: MUST BE MARRIED BY 4TH LEVEL. Otherwise the priest is guilty of a "betrayal of goals" — see PHBR3 p.121
priesthoods.followers: At 8th level: one fifth-level priest, three third-level priests and sixteen first-level priests of the same order. May take three priests (only one third-level) of his choice on adventures. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 8th level. THE STRONGHOLD MUST BE BUILT WITH A LARGE HALL OR CHAPEL where very large weddings may take place.
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with the priests of Birth/Children, Community, Culture, Love and Race.
priesthoods.note: THIRD MARRIAGE-OR-CELIBACY VARIANT, and the strictest: married by 4TH level, where Love allows until 8th. Both are graded as betrayals of goals (p.121) rather than minor offenses. THE PRIESTHOOD OF MARRIAGE APPROVES OF LOVERS but not of lovers STAYING lovers without ever being wed - they act as marriage counselors for any couple who asks their help. THE WEAPONS represent capturing, as in capturing one’s mate, and weapons often used in the sudden defense of one’s home.

priesthoods.label: Messengers
priesthoods.genderNote: Messenger-gods are as likely to be male as female.

grantedPowers.note: FROM 1ST LEVEL TO 8TH the priest receives one additional language per level — or a nonweapon proficiency slot usable only for languages. The language chosen must be that of a sentient humanoid race

priesthoods.restrictArmor: No metal armor
priesthoods.restrictClothing: WHEN ON DUTY, priests of this order must always carry sceptres, staves, poles or banners/flags on poles indicating their status
priesthoods.restrictions: WHEN CARRYING MESSAGES IN THEIR OFFICIAL CAPACITY these priests carry no obvious weapons at all. If attacked, however, they may use a sceptre as a club and a staff or pole as a quarterstaff
duties: Missions of communication: conveying important letters or verbal messages, often at the request of rulers, who require their temples to go on such missions
Acting as negotiators between two warring groups or nations
priesthoods.followers: At 8th level: five third-level priests and five first-level priests of the same order (most act as messengers too), plus one third-level bard and one third-level thief who act as fact-finders and agents, and eight Normal Men and Women all with the Reading/Writing nonweapon proficiency. May take two priests, the bard, the thief and two Normal Men and Women on adventures. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 8th level. THE STRONGHOLD MUST BE BUILT WITH A LARGE LIBRARY where the accumulated correspondence and diplomatic writing of the order accumulates.
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with the priests of Community, Mischief/Trickery, Peace, Rulership, Trade and War. Also a favorite god of heralds, spies and bards, all of whom perform messenger-duties at one time or another.
priesthoods.note: A RESTRICTION SHAPE NEW TO THE FILE: not a limit on which weapons are permitted, but on CARRYING them while on duty - "these priests carry no obvious weapons at all." The regalia they are REQUIRED to carry then doubles as their armament: a sceptre serves as a club, a staff or pole as a quarterstaff. So restrictClothing and restrictions interlock here, and both must be read alongside weaponsPermitted. FOURTH LANGUAGE GRANT, matching Literature/Poetry exactly - 1st to 8th, sentient humanoid races only. Magic remains the only one that also permits animal communication. The priests take great pride in their role as NEUTRAL conveyers of information, and in the reputation for accuracy and honesty they enjoy.

priesthoods.label: Metalwork
priesthoods.genderNote: The god of metalworking is male.
nwpRequired: Any one of: Artistic Ability (Jewelwright), Goldsmith, Silversmith, Blacksmithing, Armorer, Weaponsmithing
nwpRecommended: Any of the others from the required list

grantedPowers.note: Of workmanship quality in metal goods — tells whether a metal craft-good is of poor, average or superior quality. Gives +2 to an Appraising check if he has that proficiency, but does not by itself let him rate goods in gold pieces
Of Restriction/Obstacle — the priest can pass unharmed through the wall of fire spell
PERMANENT +2 to hit AND +2 damage with the warhammer, above and beyond all other bonuses

priesthoods.restrictArmor: METAL ARMOR ONLY — the inverse of the usual priestly restriction
duties: Education: teaching metalworking to the flock; promotion of weaponmaking, armormaking, goldsmithing and jewelrymaking, and all other sorts of metalwork in the community and society
Participation in semiannual events where metal goods of all sorts are displayed and promoted, before the throne or in market
Investigation: seeking to re-discover lost metalwork techniques, which often leads into ancient sites on expeditions of discovery
Encouraging competitive thinking between guilds, or between the metalworkers of different cities
priesthoods.followers: At 7th level: two third-level priests and four first-level priests of the same order, one third-level fighter and seven first-level fighters as temple guards, and twenty Normal Men and Women each with an appropriate and helpful nonweapon proficiency (especially Blacksmithing, Fire-building, Mining and Reading/Writing). May take one priest, one fighter and four Normal Men and Women on adventures. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 7th level. THE STRONGHOLD MUST BE BUILT WITH NUMEROUS SMITHIES AND WORKSHOPS, enough at least for the priests who do metalwork as well as the temple’s Normal Men and Women.
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with the priests of Arts, Crafts, Divinity of Mankind, Fire, Literature/Poetry, Music/Dance, Race (Dwarf), Strength and War.
priesthoods.note: THE LARGEST ALWAYS-ON COMBAT BONUS IN THE FILE: permanent +2 to hit AND +2 damage with the warhammer, above and beyond all other bonuses. Compare Hunting’s +2 to hit with bows (no damage bonus) and Good’s +1/+1 vs. evil enemies only. The warhammer is also this priesthood’s REQUIRED weapon proficiency, so the bonus always applies to something he has. SECOND INVERTED ARMOR RESTRICTION, after Fire: metal armor ONLY. Both are forge-adjacent gods. PAIRS WITH CRAFTS BY DESIGN - Crafts is the god of NON-metal goods and has a matching workmanship Analysis power with identical wording and the same +2 Appraising rider.

priesthoods.label: Mischief, Trickery
priesthoods.genderNote: The god of mischief is male.
priesthoods.armorPermitted: All non-magical non-metal armor; no shields

grantedPowers.note: Detect Secret Doors, same as the Elf ability: 1 on 1d6 passing within 10 feet, 1-2 to find secret doors and 1-3 to find concealed portals when actively searching. ELVEN priests of this order succeed on 1-2 passing within 10 feet, 1-3 to find secret doors and 1-4 for concealed portals
The DM chooses the three animal forms, or may allow the player to make the choice

priesthoods.restrictArmor: No metal armor; no magical armor; no shields
duties: Missions: priests often choose to go on adventures where they will have the opportunity to participate in some great plot or caper — it can be a deadly serious mission, so long as the priest gets to be involved in intricate planning and clever tactics
Vigilance against forces (mostly of society) that make people too responsible too young, that mature them too quickly
priesthoods.followers: At 9th level: one third-level priest and seven first-level priests of the same order, one fifth-level thief and one fifth-level bard who act as assistant mischief-makers and accompany the priest everywhere, and one third-level fighter and seven first-level fighters as guards. May take one priest, the thief, the bard and one fighter on adventures. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 9th level.
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with the priests of Fortune/Luck, Messengers, Race (Gnome), Race (Halfling), Trade, War and Wisdom. Sometimes allies of the priests of the philosophy of Evil, at DM discretion. Dislikes the priests of Strength.
priesthoods.note: THE WIDEST ALIGNMENT RANGE IN THE FILE: six of the nine, all chaotic and all neutral options. Evil priests have their own sect. A CHARACTER NEED NOT BE NASTY OR MEAN to be a priest of this god - the book is explicit that he might demonstrate cleverness through sleight of hand or by executing clever plots that STRAIGHTEN OUT problems rather than cause them. Whether he is a troublemaker is left to the player. Also the favorite god of rogues, especially thieves - but not a god of cowards.

priesthoods.label: Moon
priesthoods.genderNote: Most moon-gods are female.
priesthoods.armorPermitted: All non-metal armor; any shield that is circular or crescent-shaped

grantedPowers.note: Infravision, same as the elf ability. An elven or half-elven priest of this faith has infravision of DOUBLED range, to 120 feet
Chariot of Sustarre once per day, in addition to his other spells

priesthoods.restrictArmor: No metal armor. SHIELDS MUST BE CIRCULAR OR CRESCENT-SHAPED — a restriction on the shield’s SHAPE, not its material
duties: Education: helping in the promotion and teaching of magic
Participation in celebrations of the god, which take place once each moon — different temples may celebrate on the full moon or the new moon, at the DM’s option
priesthoods.followers: At 9th level: one fifth-level priest, three third-level priests and six first-level priests of the same order, plus one third-level mage and two first-level mages as consultants, and one third-level fighter and two first-level fighters as guards. May take two priests, one mage and one fighter on adventures. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 9th level.
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with the priests of Darkness/Night, Dawn, Hunting, Light, Magic, Oracles/Prophecy and Sun.
priesthoods.note: A SHIELD-SHAPE RESTRICTION, new to the file: "any shield that is circular or crescent-shaped." Every other shield restriction so far has been about material or about having none at all. Nothing in core_armor.json records shield shape, so this can only ever be advisory text. THE BOW REPRESENTS THE INSPIRATION OF LIGHT-SHAFTS, the same reasoning the book gives for Dawn and Light - a third entry in that family. Evil priests have their own sect. In a fantasy setting there could be numerous gods of the moon, one for each of several moons the planet possesses.

priesthoods.label: Music, Dance
priesthoods.genderNote: A god encompassing ALL aspects of music and dance is probably male. Gods of individual aspects are more likely female.
nwpRequired: Any one of: Dancing, Singing, Musical Instrument
nwpRecommended: Any of the others from the required list

grantedPowers.note: AT 5TH LEVEL this power may be used six times per day instead of three
Same as the cleric ability

priesthoods.restrictArmor: No armor of any kind; no shields
duties: Education: encouraging and supporting members of the flock, or of the general population, who show signs of talent with dance or music
priesthoods.followers: At 7th level: three third-level priests and six first-level priests of the same order, plus five first-level fighters as temple guards, and twenty Normal Men and Women each with a nonweapon proficiency appropriate to the temple (Artistic Ability, Dancing, Singing, Musical Instrument). May take three priests (only one third-level), two fighters and four Normal Men and Women on adventures. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 7th level. ONE OF THE ELEMENTS OF THE STRONGHOLD MUST BE A HALL INCLUDING A STAGE, where musicians and dancers from the surrounding area may congregate to practice their arts.
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with the priests of Arts, Community, Crafts, Culture, Divinity of Mankind, Light, Literature/Poetry, Metalwork and Sun.
priesthoods.note: THE FILE’S FIRST PRIME-REQUISITE CHOICE: "Wisdom 12 and either Charisma or Dexterity 14." primeReq2 is deliberately left EMPTY and the choice recorded in primeReq2Choice - see that README entry. APPLYING THIS TEMPLATE LEAVES SECOND PRIME REQUISITE UNSET and the player must pick Charisma or Dexterity himself. FIFTH SIX-SIDED HIT DIE, after Peace, Arts, Dawn and Literature/Poetry - all of them poor or medium combat and artistic or contemplative in theme. SOOTHING WORD IS UPGRADED RATHER THAN GAINED AT 5TH LEVEL: six uses per day instead of three. That is a different shape from every other level-gated power in the file, which arrive whole at their level; recorded in the power’s note rather than as a second entry. THE WEAPONS PERMITTED are the ones best suited to inclusion in dances.

priesthoods.label: Nature
priesthoods.genderNote: Nature-gods may be male or female.

grantedPowers.note: THE PRIEST HAS NO SPECIAL DETECTION POWERS. When he sees a plant or animal he can identify its species and whether or not it is normal for that area. He can only identify NON-MAGICAL animals and plants; those with any magical powers, including breath weapons, are beyond his power
As analysis, same scope and same limits
Same as the cleric ability
The DM can decide whether the priest turns into one animal or three, and what species he may turn into. He may opt to let the player make that choice

priesthoods.restrictions: MUST LIVE OUTSIDE CITY WALLS. Temples operated by these priests must be built outside city walls, and the priest’s permanent residence must be outside the city limits. He may SLEEP within city walls, especially when travelling or when the city is under siege. Taking permanent residence elsewhere is a MINOR OFFENSE (PHBR3 p.120), so the god withholds some of his spells the following day
duties: Vigilance against any forces, gods or mortals that threaten nature — if a god of fire has gotten too happy and is burning up great tracts of plain or forest during an overlong summer, or if a mortal civilization is destroying wilderness by exploiting it or expanding into it, priests of the god of nature are commanded (by their temple or by their god) to go forth and do something about it
priesthoods.followers: At 8th level: one fifth-level priest, three third-level priests and six first-level priests of the same order, plus two third-level rangers and four first-level rangers as guards. May take two priests and two rangers of his choice on adventures. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 8th level.
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with Druids and the priests of Agriculture, Animals, Death, Earth, Fertility, Life-Death-Rebirth Cycle, Lightning, Race (Elf), Seasons, Sky/Weather, Thunder and Vegetation.
priesthoods.note: A RESIDENCE RESTRICTION, new to the file: temples must be OUTSIDE city walls and the priest’s permanent residence outside the city limits. He may sleep within the walls when travelling or during a siege. The book grades violation explicitly as a MINOR OFFENSE (p.120), so the god withholds some spells the next day - the second entry after Life-Death-Rebirth Cycle to name that tier rather than the Betrayal ladder. Recorded in restrictions since none of the seven named categories covers where a priest lives. THE ANALYSIS/IDENTIFICATION POWER IS EXPLICITLY LIMITED, and the book says so up front: "The priest has no special detection powers." Non-magical plants and animals only - anything with magical powers, including breath weapons, is beyond him. ONLY THREE PERMITTED WEAPONS but ALL armor and shields, which is what carries it to Medium combat abilities rather than Poor.

priesthoods.label: Oceans, Rivers
priesthoods.genderNote: Sea-gods are just as likely to be male as female.

grantedPowers.note: Water breathing on himself once per day, in addition to all other spells. AT 8TH LEVEL the duration when cast on himself becomes 24 hours, and he may then cast an extra water breathing on others (normal rules) in addition to all other spells. The self-cast water breathing may not be dispelled, and at 8th level automatically renews itself at the end of the 24-hour period if he is still underwater and asleep, unconscious, etc.
Determine approximate depth UNDERWATER on 1-4 on 1d6, similar to the Dwarf ability concerning depth underground
Infravision, same as the elf ability, BUT ONLY WORKS UNDERWATER. An elven or half-elven priest of this faith has infravision of doubled range, to 120 feet, only underwater

FROM 5TH TO 8TH LEVEL the priest receives one extra language or communication — or a nonweapon proficiency slot usable only for languages — which can only be taken for AQUATIC BEINGS: aquatic elves, porpoises, mermen and the like
The DM may choose one animal or three, and which animals, or give the choice to the player — but they MUST be marine animals

priesthoods.restrictArmor: NO ARMOR of any kind, though all shields are permitted
priesthoods.followers: At 8th level: one fifth-level priest, three third-level priests and six first-level priests from the same order, plus five mermen and mermaids in total. THE DM MAY SUBSTITUTE any other intelligent aquatic race, from 5 to 10 total HD of them — aquatic elves, water-nymphs and the like. May take two priests on adventures; on WATERBORNE adventures he can take three of the mermen and mermaids, or up to 6 HD of the substituted aquatic races. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 8th level.
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with the priests of Animals (aquatic animals only) and Sky/Weather. The priests of Fire are not fond of, but not enemies of, these priests.
priesthoods.note: THE MOST HEAVILY QUALIFIED SPHERE ENTRY IN THE FILE - three separate Special Notes narrow what the granted spheres actually deliver, and NONE of them can be expressed by spheresMajor/spheresMinor or even by spheresReversed: (1) ANIMAL sphere is limited to SEA animals - he can make friends with, become invisible to, charm, speak with, hold or summon sea-life only, and cannot use the insect-related spells at all. (2) ELEMENTAL sphere is limited to spells with the word "water" in the name, plus earthquake and transmute rock to mud. (3) He may take a spell identical to the 6th-level conjure fire elemental which conjures WATER elementals instead. Encoded as all four Elemental spheres because the water restriction plus those two named earth spells does not map onto the four-way split - read this note before trusting the array. ARMOR IS INVERTED IN AN UNUSUAL WAY: no armor at all, but ALL shields permitted. Every other no-armor priesthood in the file also bars shields. THE LANGUAGE GRANT IS THE NARROWEST OF THE FIVE: 5th to 8th level only, and restricted to aquatic beings.

priesthoods.label: Oracles, Prophecy
priesthoods.genderNote: The oracular god is as likely to be male as female.

weaponsChoose.constraint: The DM chooses based on other attributes or characteristics of the oracular god. Daikyu and shuriken are also included among the choices in oriental campaigns

grantedPowers.note: FROM 1ST LEVEL TO 8TH the priest receives one extra language per level — or one extra nonweapon proficiency slot usable only for languages. These languages may only be those of sentient humanoids

priesthoods.restrictArmor: No armor of any kind; no shields
duties: Missions: having passed on a prophecy, the priest may choose to accompany those who received it — either to see how reality matches the vision, or, if the prophecy included options or visions of different resolutions, to help the preferred outcome take place
priesthoods.followers: At 9th level: one fifth-level priest, three third-level priests and six first-level priests of the same order, plus five second-level fighters as guards. May take three priests (not the fifth-level one, and only one third-level) and two fighters on adventures. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 9th level. PART OF THE STRONGHOLD MUST BE AN ORACULAR CHAMBER or area where visitors may meet the priests and receive oracles. The temple may charge a fee in money or goods for this service, so the stronghold must also have large, commodious storerooms for those goods.
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with the priests of Darkness/Night, Dawn, Fate/Destiny, Light, Magic, Moon, Sun and Wisdom.
priesthoods.note: THE ENTIRE WEAPON LIST IS A CHOICE - the first entry in the file with an EMPTY weaponsPermitted and everything in weaponsChoose. "Choose two from the following list (DM chooses based on other attributes or characteristics of the oracular god)." Fifteen options, seventeen in oriental campaigns. DISTINCT FROM FATE/DESTINY, and the book says so: this god does not preach a doctrine of acceptance, he just passes on the visions he has of the future and lets his followers and those who beg his visions act on them accordingly. SIXTH LANGUAGE GRANT: 1st to 8th, sentient humanoids only - matching Literature/Poetry and Messengers exactly.

priesthoods.label: Peace
priesthoods.genderNote: A god of peace is as likely to be male as female.

grantedPowers.note: FROM 1ST LEVEL TO 4TH the priest receives one extra language per level — or one extra nonweapon proficiency slot usable only for languages. The language chosen must be that of a sentient humanoid race
Same as the paladin ability

priesthoods.restrictArmor: All non-magical armor and shields; nothing magical
priesthoods.restrictClothing: Clothing or badges displaying priestly status whenever in public
duties: Missions: the priest often accompanies parties of war or groups of adventurers to try to bring about peaceful solutions to as many situations as possible
Vigilance against forces or individuals who seem to stir up trouble continually and needlessly

priesthoods.note: SPLIT FROM ONE BOOK ENTRY INTO SIX. PHBR3 p.80 prints "Race" as a single priesthood whose weapons, armor, spheres, followers, symbols and allied priesthoods ALL vary by race. Six template entries rather than one, because a template exists to be applied to a character and nobody is a priest of "Race" generically - and because every other entry in the book cites them individually as Race (Elven), Race (Halfling) and so on, as does the Amazon Priestess kit. Shared fields are identical across all six and duplicated deliberately. ONLY THE MATCHING RACE MAY SERVE: "Only dwarves can be priests of the god of the dwarven race, only elves can be priests of the god of the elven race." THE HALF-ELF IS THE BOOK’S STATED EXCEPTION: a half-elf may be a priest of the god of the elven race, of the human race, OR of the half-elven race. If he serves the elven god he follows the ELVEN guidelines rather than the half-elven ones; if the human god, the human guidelines. HEALING IS EXPLICITLY UNRESTRICTED BY RACE, and the book flags it as an Important Note: "There is no limitation on whom these racial priests can heal. A dwarf-race priest can heal anyone he chooses - humans, half-elves, gnomes, halflings, even elves. Of course, racial prejudice might prompt the priest to deny healing to those of another race... but that’s his individual choice, not a requirement of his faith." THE BOOK WARNS ABOUT THESE PRIESTHOODS AT THE TABLE: "The DM should be careful when letting race-oriented priests in his campaign. It’s not difficult for new or inexperienced players to misinterpret this class as a priesthood of prejudice, which is not the intent at all. These priests are supposed to support and celebrate the virtues of their own race, but NOT to be nasty to other races, contribute to stereotypes about them, exalt in jokes about them, etc. There may be priests like that in any order, but they should be NPCs who are not liked or appreciated by their fellows." THE DM MAY CREATE MORE: the book suggests a racial priesthood for the Aquatic Elf, similar to the Elf but using the weapons available to priests of oceans and rivers, or one for the desert-dwelling human where sabres, horse-back riding, desert survival and no armor are the order of the day.
