from: ONE lesser weapon from: Club, Dagger/dirk, Hand/throwing axe, Javelin, Light crossbow, Mace, Short bow, Warhammer
ONE greater weapon from: Battle axe, Heavy crossbow, Long bow, Morning star, Polearm, Quarterstaff, Spear, Sword/long
weaponsChoose.constraint: TWO SEPARATE CHOICES, one lesser and one greater. The DM makes the choice based on the history and attributes of the holy site; often the choices will be paired, such as dagger and long sword, or throwing axe and battle axe

grantedPowers.note: Granted by the god to help the priest keep the site clear of those who would harm or despoil it

priesthoods.restrictArmor: No magical armor or shields
duties: Missions: if the site is threatened, the priest will be dispatched to help straighten out the situation
priesthoods.followers: At 8th level: three third-level priests and six first-level priests of the same order, plus one fifth-level fighter, two third-level fighters and four first-level fighters who act as guards for the site and the chief priest. May take three priests (only two of whom can be third-level) and one fighter of his choice on adventures. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 8th level.
symbols: A silhouette representing the site — if it is a mountain, the silhouette of the mountain
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with the priests of Ancestors and Community.
priesthoods.note: A THIRD PC WARNING, after Disease and Peace, and this one is about PLAYABILITY rather than party harmony: "the priests seldom leave those sites, and so this is not usually a good choice for a player-character. Only when the site is threatened by distant powers is the priest allowed to leave the site for adventures." SECOND DOUBLE WEAPON CHOICE, after Rulership/Kingship - one lesser weapon and one greater, DM-chosen from the history and attributes of the holy site, and the book suggests pairing them thematically (dagger and long sword, throwing axe and battle axe). NO GUIDANCE DUTY, which is nearly unique in the file - these priests guard a place rather than a flock. ALIGNMENT SPLITS INTO TWO CULTS: neutral evil priests gather in one, neutral and neutral good in a second, and they will not be friendly to one another. The DM may instead decide a particular site deity is neutral good, in which case there are no evil priests or flock, or neutral evil, in which case no good ones. THE SITES NEED NOT BE OCCUPIED: a mountain, a cave, a plain or a valley. Usually minor gods, one god to a site, and generally the sites are famous BECAUSE they are the dwellings of gods - however, the gods seldom let themselves be seen.

priesthoods.label: Sky, Weather
priesthoods.genderNote: The sky-god is almost always male.
priesthoods.restrictArmor: No metal armor
priesthoods.followers: At 8th level: one fifth-level priest, three third-level priests and sixteen first-level priests of the same order. May take ANY THREE priests of his choice on adventures. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 8th level.
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with Druids and the priests of Agriculture, Earth, Elemental Forces, Fertility, Life-Death-Rebirth Cycle, Lightning, Nature, Oceans/Rivers, Seasons, Thunder, Vegetation and Wind.
priesthoods.note: ELEMENTAL SPHERE IS PARTIAL: only spells with the words Water, Air and Wind in their names, plus chariot of Sustarre. Encoded as all four Elemental spheres because water-and-air plus a fire-named spell does not map onto the four-way split - read this note before trusting the array. Fifth partial-Elemental case after Dawn, Fire, Lightning and Oceans/Rivers. THE PARENT OF THREE OTHER PRIESTHOODS IN THIS FILE: the book says the gods of Lightning, Thunder and Wind "can be considered lesser sky- and weather-gods", so a DM building a pantheon may want them as aspects of one deity rather than four separate gods. THE PRIESTS ARE UNUSUALLY UNBURDENED: "His priests primarily work to ensure that he receives the worship that he is due. Beyond that, they may do much as they please, serving individual communities or adventuring as they choose." Two duties only, and the followers list lets him take ANY three priests rather than restricting by level as most entries do.

priesthoods.label: Strength
priesthoods.genderNote: The strength-god is male.

grantedPowers.note: To UNDEAD LIFE-DRAINING AND PARALYSIS, and to the spells chill touch, energy drain, enervation, ray of enfeeblement and vampiric touch
Same as the cleric ability

duties: Missions: the priest is not required to, but is almost always allowed to go on adventures where he will be able to display his personal strength and demonstrate the attributes of his god
priesthoods.followers: At 8th level: three third-level priests and six first-level priests of the same order, plus one fifth-level fighter, two third-level fighters and four first-level fighters, ALL WITH A STRENGTH SCORE OF 16. May take three priests (only one third-level) and four fighters of his choice on adventures. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 8th level.
symbols: Human Silhouette Holding Up Mountain or Temple
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with the priests of Competition, Divinity of Mankind, Guardianship, Lightning, Metalwork, Thunder and War. Dislikes the priests of Death, Disease and Mischief/Trickery.
priesthoods.note: THE HIGHEST ABILITY MINIMUM IN THE FILE: Strength 15, alongside Wisdom 9. Only Disease’s Constitution 15 matches it. THE IMMUNITY IS THE MOST SPECIFICALLY ENUMERATED IN THE FILE - not a category but a named list: undead life-draining and paralysis, plus chill touch, energy drain, enervation, ray of enfeeblement and vampiric touch. Every one of them attacks Strength or vitality, which is the thematic logic. FOLLOWERS ARE FILTERED BY ABILITY SCORE, unique in the file: all seven fighters must have a Strength of 16. The god celebrates "physical strength, and nothing but strength", and his priests promote physical fitness and contests of strength such as weight-throws and wrestling, in association with priests of the god of competition. Evil priests have their own sect, and the FLOCK dislikes the priests of the god of disease, "which is a god of weakness."

priesthoods.label: Sun
priesthoods.genderNote: The sun-god is usually male.

grantedPowers.note: Detect Secret Doors, same as the Elf ability: 1 on 1d6 passing within 10 feet, 1-2 to find secret doors and 1-3 to find concealed portals when actively searching. ELVEN priests of this order succeed on 1-2 passing within 10 feet, 1-3 to find secret doors and 1-4 for concealed portals
Infravision, same as the elf ability. An elven or half-elven priest of this faith has infravision of DOUBLED range, to 120 feet
Same as the cleric ability
Same as the paladin ability
Chariot of Sustarre once per day, in addition to his other spells

priesthoods.restrictArmor: METAL ARMOR ONLY — the inverse of the usual priestly restriction
duties: Education: promoting the study of magic

Vigilance: the sun-god is a god of observation, of keen eyesight, of vigilance in general — all his priests are commanded to keep their eyes open and learn as much as possible about what is going on around them at all times. What they do with that knowledge, outside the context of helping their temple and preserving the worship of the god, is up to them
priesthoods.followers: At 9th level: three third-level priests and six first-level priests of the same order, plus one third-level fighter and two first-level fighters as guards, one third-level mage and two first-level mages as consultants, and one third-level bard and two first-level bards as personal bards. May take three priests (only one third-level), one fighter, one mage and one bard on adventures. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 9th level.
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with the priests of Arts, Crafts, Darkness/Night, Dawn, Elemental Forces, Fire, Healing, Hunting, Light, Literature/Poetry, Magic, Metalwork, Moon, Music/Dance and Oracles/Prophecy.
priesthoods.note: SIX GRANTED POWERS, the most of any entry in the file, staggered across 1st, 1st, 1st, 5th, 8th and 10th level. Light is the next closest with five. ELEMENTAL SPHERE IS PARTIAL: only spells with the words fire, flame, heat and pyrotechnics in the names. Encoded as all four Elemental spheres because the entry lists Elemental as a single minor access - read this note before trusting the array. Sixth partial-Elemental case. FOURTH INVERTED ARMOR RESTRICTION, after Fire, Metalwork and Rulership/Kingship: metal only. THE WEAPONS ARE ALL RANGED OR THROWABLE, "those which strike from afar, like the inspiration (or heatstroke) of the sun" - the same reasoning the book gives for Dawn, Light and Moon.

priesthoods.label: Thunder
priesthoods.genderNote: The thunder-god is male.
priesthoods.followers: At 8th level: three third-level priests and six first-level priests of the same order, plus three third-level fighters and six first-level fighters as guards. May take two priests and two fighters of his choice on adventures. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 8th level.
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with the priests of Elemental Forces, Lightning (ESPECIALLY), Nature, Race (Dwarven), Sky/Weather and Strength.
priesthoods.note: THE TWIN OF LIGHTNING, and the book says so: "very similar to the lightning-god; in campaigns where they both exist, they will probably be related, even brothers." Both are Good combat, both Warrior crossover, both require Weather Sense, both require a warhammer proficiency (Lightning allows hand/throwing axe as an alternative), and both are lesser sky-and-weather gods under Sky/Weather. FOURTH REQUIRED WEAPON PROFICIENCY in the file, and the only one shared with another entry. ALL FIVE PERMITTED WEAPONS ARE BLUDGEONING - club, mace, maul, morning star, warhammer - which is the smallest and most thematically uniform weapon list of any Good-combat priesthood here. Halflings excluded. Evil priests have their own sect. Like the lightning-god he is not much concerned with mortal affairs: he lets them worship him and grants power to his priests, but otherwise does not interfere.

priesthoods.label: Time
priesthoods.genderNote: The time-god is male.

grantedPowers.note: Of the current time and day. REGARDLESS OF HOW LONG THE PRIEST HAS BEEN underground, unconscious, or otherwise unable to observe the passage of time, he knows roughly what time it is (within the hour) and exactly what day of the year it is
Same as the paladin ability
Same as the cleric ability

priesthoods.restrictArmor: No magical armor; no shields
priesthoods.followers: At 8th level: one fifth-level priest, five third-level priests and ten first-level priests of the same order. May take two priests of his choice on adventures. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 8th level.
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with the priests of Death, Elemental Forces, Fate/Destiny, Seasons and Wisdom.
priesthoods.note: TWO PERMITTED WEAPONS ONLY - scythe and sickle - the smallest weapon list in the file, shared with no other entry. Nature has three; everything else has more. THE IDENTIFICATION POWER IS THE MOST NARROWLY USEFUL AND MOST RELIABLE IN THE FILE: he always knows the time within the hour and the day of the year exactly, no matter how long he has been underground or unconscious. No roll, no limit, no condition. DISTINCT FROM FATE/DESTINY: this god represents INEVITABILITY - "not destiny based on the will of individual gods, but the inevitability of change brought on by time." His priests preach patience, and help the flock adapt to their changing bodies, lifestyles and needs as they go through life.

priesthoods.label: Trade
priesthoods.genderNote: The trade-god is male.

grantedPowers.note: AUTOMATICALLY SUCCESSFUL saving throw vs. all spells with the word CHARM in the name
FROM 1ST LEVEL TO 4TH the priest receives one extra language per level — or one extra nonweapon proficiency slot usable only for languages. The languages chosen must be those of sentient humanoids

priesthoods.restrictArmor: No metal armor; no shields
priesthoods.followers: At 8th level: three third-level priests and six first-level priests of the same order, plus three second-level bards and two second-level thieves as agents (eyes and ears), and one fifth-level fighter as guard. May take two priests, one bard, one thief and the fighter on adventures. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 8th level.
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with the priests of Community, Crafts, Culture, Fortune/Luck, Messengers, Mischief/Trickery and Prosperity.
priesthoods.note: SEVENTH LANGUAGE GRANT, and it matches PEACE exactly - 1st to 4th, sentient humanoids only. The five distinct bounds across seven entries are now: 1st-4th (Peace, Trade), 1st-8th sentient humanoids (Literature/Poetry, Messengers, Oracles/Prophecy), 1st-8th with animal communication (Magic), and 5th-8th aquatic only (Oceans/Rivers). A SECOND AUTO-SUCCESS IMMUNITY, after Seasons - Chapter 2 grades these as HIGH powers where the +2 version is LOW. Immunity to everything with CHARM in the name is a sharply defined category for a merchant-god: he cannot be talked into a bad bargain by magic. The god loves bargaining and characters who bargain well, and promotes the exchange of ideas between cultures through trade. His priests try to keep trade routes between nations open, free from excessive taxes, and mutually profitable. Also a suitable deity for thieves and bards, and he likes the god of mischief and trickery. Evil priests have their own sect.

priesthoods.label: Vegetation
priesthoods.genderNote: Vegetation-gods are as likely to be male as female.
priesthoods.armorPermitted: No armor; all WOODEN shields (no metal or leather)

grantedPowers.note: Of plants — the priest can identify plants of any sort with PERFECT ACCURACY
As analysis, same scope
Of Obstacle — the priest can pass through overgrown areas like the druid, but can do so AT 1ST LEVEL

priesthoods.restrictArmor: NO ARMOR of any kind. Shields must be WOODEN — no metal or leather
priesthoods.restrictClothing: MAY NOT WEAR LEATHERS OR FURS in their clothing
priesthoods.followers: At 8th level: one fifth-level priest, three third-level priests and sixteen first-level priests of the same order. May take two priests of his choice on adventures. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 8th level.
symbols: Single plant of any sort, except domestic grains
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with Druids and the priests of Agriculture, Earth, Fertility, Life-Death-Rebirth Cycle, Nature, Seasons and Sky/Weather.
priesthoods.note: THE SECOND WOODEN-SHIELDS-ONLY ENTRY, alongside Wind (p.91), and the two share a clothing restriction as well - no leathers or furs. Neither can be computed: core_armor.json records no shield material, because no 2e source splits shields that way. Both are advisory text. ITS SYMBOL CARRIES AN EXCLUSION: any single plant EXCEPT domestic grains, which belong to the god of Agriculture. DEFIANCE OF OBSTACLE AT 1ST LEVEL is called out as better than the druid’s equivalent, which arrives later. The god admires wild growth specifically - plant-life "which is wild and not fettered or trimmed or tamed by mankind" - and his priests work to keep civilization from making inroads into wilderness, spreading tales of the forest as deep and dangerous, sneaking around in the wilderness casting spells on travelling city-folk, and stocking forests with dangerous animals to reinforce the impression. THEY DO NOT IMPEDE those who know the forest - elves, gnomes, rangers, hunters, trappers, woodsmen - but WILL terrorize innocents and city-soft travellers.

priesthoods.label: War
priesthoods.genderNote: The chief war-god is male, but lesser war-gods are as likely to be female as male.
wpRequired: No specific weapon, but the priest must choose ONE from his permitted list and specialize in it
priesthoods.restrictWeapons: Must choose one weapon from the permitted list and specialize in it — the ONLY priest in the book who may take any weapon specialization
duties: Missions: the priests want to and are required to accompany armies on the march of war; at every war, priests of this sect attend the officers and rulers of BOTH sides
Vigilance against complacency and the tide of philosophies of peacefulness — if a land is too peaceful for too long, they must shake things up and get a war, even a small one, going
priesthoods.followers: At 8th level: one fifth-level priest, three third-level priests and six first-level priests of the same order, plus two fifth-level fighters as guards. May take three priests of his choice and one fighter on adventures. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 8th level. THE STRONGHOLD MUST INCLUDE A LARGE ARMORY CHAMBER.
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with the priests of Community, Culture, Guardianship, Justice/Revenge, Messengers, Metalwork, Mischief/Trickery and Rulership/Kingship. Dislikes the priests of Peace.
priesthoods.note: THE ONLY PRIESTHOOD IN THE BOOK PERMITTED WEAPON SPECIALIZATION: "He is the only priest who can take any weapon specialization." It is MANDATORY, not optional - he must choose one weapon from his permitted list and specialize in it according to normal weapon specialization rules. Chris’s ruling (see project notes): that means the WHOLE package including the Table 35 attack progression, since the PHB’s "single-class fighters only" is the exact restriction PHBR3 lifts. EACH NATION HAS ITS OWN CULT and they do not cooperate in wartime, especially when their armies are opposed. In peacetime they may cooperate - but usually only to conspire and start another war. Lesser war-gods would be gods of a secondary aspect: Berserker Rages, Battlefield Terror, Confusion, Tactics, Cavalry. Evil priests have their own sect.

priesthoods.label: Wind
priesthoods.genderNote: Wind-gods are male.

grantedPowers.note: Into ONE bird form of the DM’s choice — the DM may allow the player to choose the bird form
Aerial servant once per day, in addition to all his other spells

priesthoods.restrictArmor: No shields
priesthoods.followers: At 8th level: one fifth-level priest, three third-level priests and six first-level priests of the same order, plus ten first-level fighters to serve as guards. May take ANY three priests and four fighters of his choice on adventures. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 8th level.
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with the priests of Sky/Weather.
priesthoods.note: CORRECTED. THIS ENTRY PREVIOUSLY HELD VEGETATION’S DATA. It was seeded at the start of transcription from book p.90, whose left column is the TAIL of the Vegetation entry while the "Wind" heading sits on p.91 - the same column-break error that hit elemental_forces twice. It went undetected because the entry stayed marked partial and was never re-read. Wind is GOOD combat with all armor and sixteen weapons; Vegetation is POOR combat with no armor and four. Nothing carried over. ELEMENTAL SPHERE IS SEVERELY LIMITED and the book says so: only dust devil, air walk, chariot of Sustarre and wind walk - FOUR NAMED SPELLS. "The priest gets an extra major access to make up for the severe limitation imposed on his Elemental sphere access." Encoded as all four Elemental spheres because a four-spell whitelist cannot be expressed; read this note before trusting the array. Seventh and most extreme partial-Elemental case. A LESSER SKY-AND-WEATHER GOD, per Sky/Weather p.86, alongside Lightning and Thunder. Lesser wind-gods would represent specific winds: the cold north wind, the balmy southern wind, the terrifying typhoon or hurricane, the incredibly destructive tornado. SAILORS ESPECIALLY PRAY TO THESE GODS for good winds; the gods are playful and sometimes malicious, and may choose to blow ships wildly off-course. The priests make these prayers for friendly winds, but are otherwise left much to their own devices, and many are adventurers and hero-sailors.

priesthoods.label: Wisdom
priesthoods.genderNote: The god of wisdom will be female.

grantedPowers.note: To the confusion and feeblemind spells

duties: Education: this sect believes in education for its own sake, and works to provide teaching to all the flock and even the general population when possible
Vigilance: these priests try to act as advisors to rulers, in order to keep them from making decisions in a too-hasty or foolish fashion — and local rulers often DO give them posts as advisors
priesthoods.followers: At 9th level: two third-level priests and four first-level priests of the same order, plus one fifth-level fighter, one third-level fighter and two second-level fighters as guards, and one third-level mage, one third-level bard, one second-level thief and one second-level illusionist as consultants. May take two priests (only one third-level), two fighters of his choice, and two from the mage, bard, thief and illusionist. Priesthood pays half the stronghold cost at 9th level.
priesthoods.relations: Good terms with the priests of Divinity of Mankind, Good, Literature/Poetry, Mischief/Trickery, Oracles/Prophecy and Time. Dislikes the priests of Evil, whom they do not consider sensible.
priesthoods.note: THE LAST ENTRY IN CHAPTER 3, and the one whose ability requirement is the point: Wisdom 13 alone, no second prime requisite, and no other minimum. THE IMMUNITY IS NAMED RATHER THAN CATEGORICAL - confusion and feeblemind specifically, the two spells that take a mind away. Thematically the tightest immunity in the file. WISDOM IS DISTINCT FROM EDUCATION, and the book is careful about it: "It consists merely of having sense enough to know what it otherwise takes experience or an education to learn. The learned man knows from experience when his words will provoke a fight; the wise man knows it intuitively, instinctively." NOT A GOD OF PEACE: its priests will often be advisors to military officers, helping them plan effective strategies. They promote sensible solutions, suggest compromises and alternatives, plan future events, and look for trouble in upcoming events to head it off.
